## Titanium Dioxide

Titanium Dioxide (TiO₂) is a brilliant white inorganic pigment valued for its exceptional opacity, high refractive index, and stability . It is considered the world's most important white pigment, serving as a critical component in a vast array of products by providing outstanding whiteness, brightness, and hiding power

* Synonyms:

  Titania; Titanium(IV) oxide; TiO₂
* Formula:

  TiO₂
* CAS NO.:

  13463-67-7
* Package:

  25KG BAG
* Certificate:

  Reach, ISO9001

Our Achievement

**Global Reach:**Our  Titanium Dioxide has been successfully exported and applied in key markets across the globe, including but not limited to UAE, Thailand, Vietnam, Egypt, Brazil  etc.  Our product has consistent quality and ability to meet diverse international standards.

**Equivalent Alternatives:**We supply different brands of Titanium Dioxide, including Lomon billions, Taihai, panzhihua etc, and both rutile and anatase like R996, R5566, R218 etc, helping customers reduce costs with comparable (or even superior) results in performance.

Key Applications

* •Paints, Coatings, and Inks
* •Plastics and Rubber
* •Paper and Printing
* •Cosmetics and Personal Care

The main detailed uses of the product

* ![Paints, Coatings, and Inks](//vhost-ln-s06-cdn.hcwebsite.com/fa7e31b4953e04fc98064531b93c9816/tpl/en_achilleschem/assets/app/images/imgload.png?v=C8Ksg47k)

  Paints, Coatings, and Inks

  TiO₂ is a fundamental ingredient in architectural and industrial paints, providing excellent covering power (opacity), durability, and gloss . Its resistance to UV light makes it essential for exterior coatings that require long-term weather ability .
* ![Plastics and Rubber](//vhost-ln-s06-cdn.hcwebsite.com/fa7e31b4953e04fc98064531b93c9816/tpl/en_achilleschem/assets/app/images/imgload.png?v=C8Ksg47k)

  Plastics and Rubber

  In the plastics industry, TiO₂ is used to impart whiteness, opacity, and enhanced mechanical properties to products ranging from packaging to automotive parts . It improves heat resistance and weatherability in plastics and rubber applications .
* ![Paper and Printing](//vhost-ln-s06-cdn.hcwebsite.com/fa7e31b4953e04fc98064531b93c9816/tpl/en_achilleschem/assets/app/images/imgload.png?v=C8Ksg47k)

# European Coatings Show: Product Spotlight

* Topic: [CoatingsTech Update](https://www.paint.org/coatingstech-magazine/topics/coatingstech-updates/), [Conferences](https://www.paint.org/coatingstech-magazine/topics/conferences/), [New Products](https://www.paint.org/coatingstech-magazine/topics/new-products/)

[![Open paint cans](https://www.paint.org/wp-content/uploads/2020/10/OCT15_paint-cans.jpg)](https://www.paint.org/coatingstech-magazine/articles/european-coatings-show-product-spotlight/)

Share via:

* [Facebook](#)
* [Twitter](#)
* [LinkedIn](#)
* [Print](#)

*Editor’s note: This column is a roundup of product releases to be highlighted at the [2023 European Coatings Show](https://www.european-coatings-show.com/) (ECS) in Nuremberg, Germany. To submit a product release for consideration, email [aelliot@paint.org](mailto:aelliot@paint.org). Please note that all submissions are subject to editorial approval and publication is not guaranteed.*

**Penn Color Dispersions**

Penn Color, supplier of colors, additives, and compounds headquartered in Hatfield, PA, will be at the upcoming ECS to present their range of dispersions, which is composed of those that are water-based, solventborne, or energy-curable.

According to the company, their water-based dispersions have low to no VOCs and high pigment loading properties and are APEO- and binder-free. The solvent-based dispersions are broadly compatible with acrylic resin systems and have high pigment-loading and optimal rheological properties. The energy-curable dispersions are for 100% solids and multiple oligomers, require low curing energy, and are broadly compatible with various systems.

Learn more about [Penn Color](https://www.penncolor.com/)’s dispersions range at Stand 2-615 in Hall 2.

**Clariant Halogen-Free Flame Retardants**

Clariant plans to showcase three product lines focused on sustainability at ECS: Ceridust® additives, EcoTain® (which includes Exolit® AP 435 and Exolit AP 418, and VITA, which includes polyglycols (PEGs) and ethylene oxide derivatives.

Clariant’s Ceridust® additives are made to enable scratch-resistant protection for packaging barrier coatings with a good slip-effect and rub-resistant printing inks. The company says these additives are free of PTFEs and include polyethylene waxes and a biobased wax.

Two products that Clariant plans to feature are from its EcoTain® sustainability line. Exolit® AP 435 is intended to prolong the shelf life of finished products during storage and transportation, and Exolit AP 418 is designed for efficiency, thus reducing the industry’s material use. The latter product, according to Clariant, can achieve up to 10% longer fire-resistant time for a film applied at up to 25% less thickness than what is typical.

The VITA range includes polyglycols (PEGs) and ethylene oxide derivatives for use as surfactants and intermediates in paint and coatings production. The company states that VITA products are 100% based on plant-based carbon via bioethanol. These new ingredients are chemically equivalent to their fossil-based analogs and therefore offer the same performance and efficiency to formulators and brand owners, according to Clariant.

[Clariant](http://www.clariant.com) will be at Booth 322 in Hall 3A.

**Heubach Coil, Green, and UV Pigments**

The Heubach Group, a German-based manufacturer of organic and inorganic pigments and preparations, will unveil several new pigments at ECS: Heucosil™ CSA and CSM, Heucodur® Green 630, and Hostatint™ UV 100.

Heucosil™ CSA and CSM are zinc-free anti-corrosive pigments that the company says meet the performance requirements for coil- and thin-film applications. These products are designed for corrosion protection performance and low oil absorption.

Heucodur® Green 630 is a new non-labeled spinel green pigment based on a chrome-free composition, and Hostatint™ UV 100 is a reformulated range of pigment preparations for radiation-cured wood coatings.

Visit [Heubach](https://www.sudarshan.com/newsroom/sudarshan-chemical-completes-acquisition-of-heubach-group/) at Booth 427 in Hall 3C to learn more about these pigments.

**Vencorex Crosslinkers, Hardeners, and Isocyanate Monomers**

Vencorex, a producer of aliphatic isocyanates and their derivatives, will unveil several products at ECS: Easaqua™, Tolonate™, and HDI and IPDI isocyanate monomers.

Easaqua™ crosslinkers are designed for 2K waterborne polyurethanes as they are easy to mix in water. Vencorex says that products in this line can be used with matte and high-gloss primers and finishes, and some have fast-drying properties.

Tolonate™ are reference polyisocyanate hardeners of high-performance polyurethane coatings and adhesives. The company says that they enable good durability and extended service life. The range includes low-viscosity grades, which are essential in the development of solvent-free and high-solids formulations, and which have low- or even zero-VOC content, according to Vencorex. The line also includes some flexible and elastic products for polyurea and polyaspartic coatings.

HDI and IPDI isocyanate monomers, used for light-stable polyurethane dispersions (PUD) and thermoplastic polyurethane (TPU) and UV-curable resins.

[Vencorex](https://www.vencorex.com/), which is headquartered in France, has three manufacturing sites in Grenoble, France; Freeport, TX; and Rayong, Thailand. Visit Booth 461 in Hall 3 to learn more.

**LB Group TiO2 Pigments**

LB Group, a Chinese chemical company, will be at ECS to introduce three products from its titanium dioxide pigment (TiO2) lines for coatings and inks: the BILLIONS™ R-996 pigment, BILLIONS™ BLR-895 pigment, and BILLIONS™ TR52.

The BILLIONS™ R-996 pigment is a sulfate-process titanium dioxide pigment designed for external and internal architectural coatings that can also be used for industrial and powder coatings. The BILLIONS™ BLR-895 pigment is a chloride-process titanium dioxide pigment that can produce a white hue with a blue undertone in external and internal architectural coatings. The BILLIONS™ TR52 pigment is a sulfate-process titanium dioxide pigment designed for printing inks.

Visit [LB Group](https://www.lomonbillions.global/) at Booth 5-465 in Hall 5.

**IFF Additives, Thickeners, and Binders**

New York-based IFF, a chemicals manufacturer, will be at ECS to talk about several of their products.

Lattice® NTC Colloidal Microcrystalline Cellulose is a functional, biodegradable fiber that is designed to improve formulation stability with low viscosity.

WALSRODER™ Nitrocellulose (NC) is IFF’s brand of printing inks, wood coatings, and varnishes. Products in the NC line are free-flowing and include an automated emptying device to enable a short emptying time (15–25 seconds per drum) and eliminate the need to manually lift a drum, according to IFF.

POLYOX™ Polyethylene Oxide is a water-soluble thickener, binder, film-forming polymer that is designed to improve adhesion.

ETHOCEL™ Ethylcellulose is a thickener and binder for solvent-based paints, wood coatings, and printing inks.

TEXTURECEL™ Carboxymethylcellulose is a thickener and binder in water-based coatings and ink formulations. The company says that the product offers thickening and rheology modification properties and is a natural alternative to synthetic polymers.

METHOCEL™ Cellulose Ethers are a key formulation component in paint removers and are soluble in water and many organic solvents.

Visit Stand 1-560 in Hall 1 to learn more about these six [IFF](https://www.iff.com/) products.

## Commercial profile

OMYA PERU S.A.C. (tax ID 20608572067, PERU) is active in foreign trade. Between 2021 and 2024 it recorded 200 operations, importing a CIF value of 7.7 million dollars (peak in 2024) and exporting a FOB value of 175.6 thousand dollars. Its imports concentrate on chemical products, plastics and rubber and minerals and fuels, sourced from China, Colombia and Netherlands; its exports on plastics and rubber, chemical products and minerals and fuels, shipped to Venezuela, Colombia and Chile. Goods move mainly through MARITIMA DEL CALLAO via marítimo.

Why does this profile matter?

As a buyer, OMYA PERU S.A.C. records 192 import operations worth 7.7 million dollars, concentrated in chemical products, plastics and rubber and minerals and fuels. Its key origins (China, Colombia and Netherlands) and purchasing recurrence make it a medium-volume account, attractive to suppliers seeking stable contracts in PERU.

As an exporter, OMYA PERU S.A.C. ships plastics and rubber, chemical products and minerals and fuels for a FOB value of 175.6 thousand dollars, with presence in markets such as Venezuela, Colombia and Chile. Its export profile positions it as a counterpart for international buyers in those destinations.

In logistics, OMYA PERU S.A.C. operates mainly via marítimo (87% of its shipments) entering mainly through MARITIMA DEL CALLAO. Its usual loading ports include BUENAVENTURA, QINGDAO and SHANGHAI. It works with customs agents such as HANSA ADUANAS SOCIEDAD ANONIMA and AGL GROUP ADUANAS S.A.C. and warehouses such as DT DINETPERU S.A.C.. Freight accounts for around 9% of the CIF value.

Financially, OMYA PERU S.A.C. accumulates a trade value of 7.8 million dollars. It pays duties of 669 dollars. With 200 operations and about 6925 tons moved, it represents a medium-value profile for commercial risk analysis and due diligence.

**B. Private Platform (Subscriber Environment):** Accessible exclusively to active clients via corporate Login. Industry Insight

## What Is Titanium Dioxide Used for in Soap Manufacturing?

Titanium Dioxide (TiO₂) is one of the most widely used functional additives in the global soap and personal care manufacturing sector. When incorporated into soap bars, liquid soaps, or specialty cleansers, TiO₂ serves as a powerful opacifying agent and whitening pigment, giving products the clean, bright white appearance that consumers associate with purity and freshness.

In bar soap production, typically 0.1%–1.0% by weight of TiO₂ is added to the saponified mass during processing. This small but effective concentration delivers extraordinary visual impact — producing a solid, opaque, pearl-white finish that is virtually impossible to replicate with alternative ingredients. Beyond aesthetics, TiO₂ acts as a mild UV scattering agent, providing a degree of formulation stability.

🔬 Key Fact: Rutile-grade TiO₂ offers a refractive index of ~2.73 — the highest of any commercially available white pigment — delivering unmatched opacity and brightness in soap formulations.

Anatase-grade TiO₂ is also widely used in soap due to its softer, bluish-white tone and mild abrasive properties, which can gently assist with skin cleansing. Leading global soap manufacturers — from mass-market brands to artisan producers — rely on high-purity TiO₂ grades to ensure consistent batch-to-batch color performance across production lines.

Technical Deep Dive

## TiO₂ in Paper Coatings: Function, Performance & Industrial Role

The paper and paperboard industry is one of the largest consumers of titanium dioxide worldwide. TiO₂ is incorporated into paper coating slurries to dramatically improve the optical properties of the final sheet — enhancing brightness, whiteness, opacity, and printability. These improvements are critical for premium printing papers, packaging materials, specialty labels, and coated boards.

In paper coating applications, TiO₂ is dispersed into an aqueous coating slurry alongside clay, calcium carbonate, binders, and other functional additives. The coating is then applied to the base paper surface via blade, rod, or curtain coating methods. The result is a smooth, highly printable surface with excellent ink holdout and light reflection properties.

📄 Industry Data: The global paper coatings TiO₂ market is projected to reach USD 4.2 billion by 2030, driven by growing demand for premium packaging, digital printing substrates, and specialty coated papers across Asia-Pacific.

Rutile TiO₂ is preferred in paper coatings due to its superior scattering efficiency, weather resistance, and photostability compared to the anatase form. Surface-treated grades with alumina and silica coatings offer enhanced dispersibility and reduced photocatalytic activity, which helps protect binders and base paper fibers from degradation over time.

Core Benefits

## Why TiO₂ Is the #1 Choice for Paper Coating & Soap

From optical performance to formulation stability, titanium dioxide delivers properties that no alternative white pigment can match at comparable cost-efficiency.

⚡

### Maximum Opacity & Hiding Power

TiO₂'s extraordinary refractive index (2.55–2.73) delivers unmatched light-scattering efficiency. In paper coatings, this translates to excellent print opacity; in soap, it produces a brilliant opaque-white bar at minimal dosage levels.

🌟

### Superior Brightness & Whiteness

High-purity rutile TiO₂ grades achieve ISO brightness values exceeding 98%, making them indispensable for premium coated papers, high-white printing stocks, and luxury soap formulations where visual aesthetics are paramount.

🛡️

### UV Protection & Durability

Rutile TiO₂ acts as an effective UV-scattering agent in both soap and paper products, helping to protect formulations from photodegradation and maintaining product appearance through prolonged exposure to light and environmental conditions.

🔄

### Excellent Dispersibility

Surface-engineered TiO₂ grades with optimized particle size distribution and surface treatments offer superior dispersion in both aqueous paper coating slurries and saponified soap matrices, ensuring batch-to-batch color consistency.

✅

### Regulatory Compliance & Safety

Food-contact and cosmetic-grade TiO₂ products comply with FDA, EU Regulation 231/2012, and ISO standards, making them suitable for both personal care soap applications and food-adjacent paper packaging substrates.

💰

### Cost-Effective Performance

Due to its exceptional scattering efficiency, TiO₂ requires lower loading levels than competing white pigments such as calcium carbonate or talc to achieve equivalent opacity — resulting in overall cost savings in formulation and raw material consumption.

Market Outlook

## Commercial & Industrial Trends: TiO₂ in Soap & Paper Coatings

The global titanium dioxide market continues to evolve, with paper coatings and personal care emerging as two of the fastest-growing consumption segments driven by premiumization, sustainability demands, and Asia-Pacific market expansion.

📈

### Asia-Pacific Market Expansion

China, India, and Southeast Asia account for over 55% of global TiO₂ demand growth in the paper sector. Rising middle-class consumption is driving demand for premium packaging, coated printing papers, and branded personal care products — all requiring higher-quality TiO₂.

♻️

### Sustainability & Green Formulations

Eco-conscious brands are driving demand for TiO₂ grades with lower environmental footprints. Manufacturers are developing chloride-process TiO₂ with reduced waste streams, and waterborne paper coating systems with optimized TiO₂ loading to minimize total pigment use.

🖨️

### Digital Printing & Specialty Paper Demand

The explosive growth of digital and inkjet printing technologies is creating new demand for ultra-smooth, high-brightness coated paper substrates. These specialty papers require precisely engineered TiO₂ grades with controlled particle size and surface chemistry for optimal ink absorption.

🧴

### Premiumization in Personal Care Soap

As consumers increasingly demand luxury, artisan, and specialty soap products, formulators are turning to high-purity cosmetic-grade TiO₂ to deliver the brilliant white aesthetics required for premium product positioning — from hotels and spas to natural and organic soap brands.

🏭

### Functional Packaging Innovation

TiO₂-coated packaging papers are gaining ground in food and pharmaceutical packaging due to their ability to provide light barrier properties, delay product oxidation, and extend shelf life — unlocking new commercial opportunities beyond traditional printing stocks.

🔬

### Nano-TiO₂ & Advanced Surface Treatments

Next-generation surface-treated and nano-scale TiO₂ formulations are being developed to achieve equal optical performance at lower pigment loading, reduce processing costs, and enable new functional properties such as antimicrobial activity in specialty soap and medical paper applications.

Application Scenarios

## Deep-Dive: TiO₂ Applications in Paper Coating & Soap

Explore the full breadth of industrial and commercial scenarios where titanium dioxide for soap and paper coatings delivers measurable performance advantages.

📰

### LWC & MWC Printing Paper Coatings

Lightweight coated (LWC) and medium-weight coated (MWC) papers for magazine printing, catalogues, and commercial advertising rely on TiO₂ to achieve the high brightness and opacity required for vibrant full-color reproduction. TiO₂ is blended with ground calcium carbonate (GCC) and kaolin to optimize cost and performance.

📦

### Premium Packaging Board Coatings

Folding boxboard, liquid packaging board (LPB), and solid bleached sulfate (SBS) board manufacturers apply TiO₂-containing coatings to achieve the brilliant white, printable surfaces required for premium food, beverage, cosmetics, and pharmaceutical packaging applications.

🏷️

### Label Stock & Self-Adhesive Papers

White opaque label papers for product labeling, pharmaceutical packaging, and logistics applications require high TiO₂ loading to provide excellent opacity over varied background colors. Precisely dispersed TiO₂ ensures consistent whiteness and print quality across label surfaces.

🧼

### Bar Soap & Syndet Bars

Traditional saponified bar soaps and modern synthetic detergent bars (syndets) both use TiO₂ as the primary whitening and opacifying agent. Grades optimized for saponification compatibility ensure uniform dispersion throughout the soap matrix without interfering with lathering or skin-feel properties.

💧

### Liquid Soap & Body Wash Formulations

Liquid soap, body wash, and shampoo bar formulations incorporate micronized or dispersed TiO₂ to create pearlescent or opaque white visual effects. The non-ionic compatibility of properly surface-treated TiO₂ makes it suitable for a broad range of surfactant-based systems.

🌿

### Natural & Organic Artisan Soap

In the rapidly growing natural and artisan soap segment, cosmetic-grade TiO₂ — particularly ultramarine-compatible and soap-safe grades — is used to achieve the clean white color needed for high-contrast swirl patterns, layered designs, and branded aesthetic presentations sought by premium handmade soap markets.

🎨

### Decorative Paper & Wallpaper Coatings

Decorative laminate papers, wallcoverings, and surface finishing papers require high-opacity TiO₂ coatings to provide consistent whiteness and excellent hiding power over the base substrate. This ensures that the decorative print or pattern above appears vivid, true-to-color, and free of substrate bleed-through.

🏥

### Medical & Pharmaceutical Paper Applications

Medical wrapping papers, drug-release matrices, and pharmaceutical leaflet papers utilize specialty TiO₂ grades to meet strict regulatory purity standards while delivering the printability and whiteness necessary for professional medical and healthcare packaging applications.

Titanium Dioxide Lomon R-996 An Overview of Manufacturers and Applications

  

Titanium dioxide (TiO2) is one of the most widely used white pigments in the world, known for its exceptional brightness and opacity. Among the various grades of titanium dioxide available on the market, Lomon R-996 stands out as a premium product, primarily manufactured by Lomon Billions Group, a leading producer of titanium dioxide.

  

What is Lomon R-996?

  

Lomon R-996 is a high-quality rutile titanium dioxide pigment that exhibits excellent whiteness, high refractive index, and outstanding durability. It is specifically designed for various applications, including paints, coatings, plastics, and paper. The product is manufactured using advanced processes that ensure consistent quality and performance, making it a preferred choice for industries that demand high standards.

  

Applications of Lomon R-996

  

One of the key attributes of Lomon R-996 is its versatility across different applications. In the paint and coatings industry, it is used to enhance the aesthetic appeal and longevity of the products. Its high opacity means that only a small amount is needed to achieve the desired coverage, thus reducing the overall cost of formulations.

  

In the plastics industry, Lomon R-996 contributes to the UV resistance of products, making it ideal for outdoor applications. This grade of titanium dioxide helps in stabilizing colors and preventing degradation caused by sunlight exposure. Similarly, in the paper industry, its usage improves the brightness and printability of paper products.

  
 [**Moreover, Lomon R-996 is suitable for other niche applications, including cosmetics and personal care products**](https://www.cqtitaniumdioxide.com/products). Its non-toxic nature and excellent dispersibility make it a safe choice for formulations in skin care and makeup products.  

Global Producers of Lomon R-996

  
[**titanium dioxide lomon r-996 manufacturers**](https://www.cqtitaniumdioxide.com/products)  
  
![titanium dioxide lomon r-996 manufacturers](https://images.exportstart.com/images/cqtitaniumdioxide/goods/7_2023051822305717781.jpg "titanium dioxide lomon r-996 manufacturers")  

While Lomon Billions Group is the primary manufacturer of Lomon R-996, several other companies also produce similar grades of titanium dioxide. These include well-known manufacturers across Europe, North America, and Asia, who offer competitive alternatives to Lomon R-996. Some of these companies have invested substantially in technology to improve the quality and sustainability of their titanium dioxide products.

  

For instance, companies like Tronox and Chemours in North America are recognized for producing high-quality TiO2 grades, albeit with slightly different properties. In Europe, companies like Venator and Huntsman also supply titanium dioxide products catering to various industrial needs.

  

Sustainability and Environmental Concerns

  

As the demand for titanium dioxide grows, manufacturers face increasing scrutiny regarding the environmental impact of their production processes. Lomon Billions Group, in particular, is committed to adopting sustainable practices in its operations. This includes reducing waste, optimizing resource utilization, and minimizing emissions from manufacturing plants.

  

The industry as a whole is moving towards more sustainable alternatives, like using recycled materials and exploring alternative raw materials. Furthermore, regulatory frameworks in various regions are pushing manufacturers toward more environmentally friendly production methods.

  

Conclusion

  

Lomon R-996 is a leading grade of titanium dioxide known for its excellent properties and wide-ranging applications. As industries continue to demand high-quality pigments, manufacturers are innovating and optimizing processes to meet these needs sustainably. As users of titanium dioxide seek reliable suppliers, Lomon R-996 from Lomon Billions Group remains a top choice among manufacturers worldwide, ensuring that products maintain their quality and performance in a competitive market.

  

In summary, the landscape of titanium dioxide production is vibrant, with Lomon R-996 exemplifying quality, versatility, and sustainability in the industry.

# TiO2 Manufacturing Process: Raw Material, Application Areas, Production Technologies

4672  14 min 8 November, 2023   ![mht-logo-square-big](https://www.mheavytechnology.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/10/mht-logo-square-big.svg)   M HEAVY TECHNOLOGY Team

## What is titanium dioxide, and what are its properties?

Titanium dioxide is one of the most essential inorganic materials modern industry consumes. It is widely used in the contemporary world and is the primary commercial product of the titanium production sector. How is titanium dioxide manufactured and utilized? We will discuss it in this article along with other relevant aspects.

Pure titanium dioxide (TiO2) is a colorless, crystalline solid substance. When heated, its crystals turn yellow, and upon cooling, they regain their colorless appearance.

Modifications of titanium dioxide include:

* Rutile (cubic syngony, 85-90% of global production);
* Brookite (orthorhombic syngony);
* Anatase (tetragonal syngony, 10-15%);
* Rhombic IV and hexagonal V modifications.

Titanium dioxide is produced in two forms: rutile (R-type) and anatase (A-type).

### **Rutile titanium dioxide**

It scatters light approximately 30% better than anatase, and it has better hiding power (the ability of titanium dioxide to cover the color of the painted surface).

Rutile titanium dioxide is preferred in paints, coatings, plastics, and cosmetics production.

### ****Anatase form****

It is less resistant to atmospheric conditions than rutile and provides less protection against UV radiation. Anatase pigments find their application in producing paper, rubber, and soap.

### ******Use of titanium depending on its properties******

Traditionally, the vast majority (about 95%) of all produced titanium dioxide is used in making paints and coatings.

The leading role of titanium dioxide among white pigments is predetermined by its high level of quality. This product is characterized by its ability to disperse, as well as its thermal and chemical resistance, whitening capability, resistance to atmospheric conditions, high refractive index, and more. These properties depend on the size of raw material particles and are significantly enhanced by their nanostructuring.

In the paint and coatings industry, the primary function of TiO2 is to impart paints with a white color and brightness and to enhance hiding power. It also protects against harmful ultraviolet rays and prevents film aging and yellowing of painted surfaces.

Titanium dioxide is a stable substance (the most stable one among all known white pigments). It is non-volatile and insoluble in acids, alkalis, and solutions under normal conditions.

Titanium dioxide is amphoteric, meaning it has basic and acidic properties (although it reacts with concentrated acids). It demonstrates high chemical stability towards various compounds, including those that may be toxic and present in the environment. Due to its inertness, titanium dioxide is non-toxic and generally considered a very safe substance. It can come into contact with packaged products and even be used as a food coloring in certain concentrations.

It may even enter the body as an aerosol through inhalation or ingestion. It is non-flammable.

Specific properties of titanium dioxide make it indispensable in various industries, contributing to the rapid growth of the global titanium dioxide market.

## World Market of Titanium Dioxide Pigment Production.

There is a high demand for titanium dioxide in the global market, which is expected to continue growing. Additionally, there is a constant increase in the worldwide need for inorganic pigments. According to experts’ estimates, in recent years, titanium dioxide pigment accounted for 65-70% of the total consumption of inorganic pigments and over 90% of the consumption of white pigments.

In 2021, the titanium dioxide market was estimated to be more than 6 million tons, and it is projected that from 2022 to 2027, the market will demonstrate an average annual growth rate of over 6%. In the short term, the rapidly growing demand from the paint and coatings industry will be the primary driver of titanium dioxide market growth.

Titanium dioxide pigment is produced in 15 countries, with 33% of production capacity located in the USA. Additionally, almost 40% of production is in China, Ukraine, Germany, the United Kingdom, Finland, Saudi Arabia, Japan, France, Australia, and other countries.

The global titanium dioxide production distribution is as follows:

China has the largest titanium dioxide production capacity, producing approximately 3 million tons annually.

The largest world producers are the following companies: DuPont Titanium Technologies (USA), National Titanium Dioxide Co., Ltd. Cristal (Saudi Arabia), Huntsman Pigments (USA), Tronox, Inc. (USA), Kronos Worldwide, Inc. (USA), Sachtleben Chemie GmbH (Germany; Rockwood Holdings own 100% of the shares), Ishihara Sangyo Kaisha, Ltd. (Japan).

## Raw materials for production of titanium dioxide pigment

A crucial aspect of the titanium dioxide manufacturing process is the supply of high-quality titanium ore. Despite titanium being one of Earth’s most abundant chemical elements, it occurs in deficient natural concentrations. Therefore, to establish an adequate supply of titanium ore capable of meeting the economic demands of TiO2 production, it is essential to implement rational methods of extraction and refinement of this mineral.

*Read more about* [*titanium ore mining and processing*](https://www.mheavytechnology.com/news/processing-titanium-ore/)*.*

### Ilmenite concentrate (FeTiO3)

The primary raw material in the titanium dioxide production process is ilmenite concentrate (FeTiO3), produced by [mining and processing](https://www.mheavytechnology.com/services/mining-processing-plant/). Ilmenite is an ore that, from a chemical perspective, is a mixture of oxides, the majority of which are titanium and iron oxides.

### Titanium slag

The second most significant raw material for the tio2 manufacturing process is titanium slag, containing 75-90% TiO2 and 5-7% FeO.

Read also our article on [titanium slag production process.](https://www.mheavytechnology.com/news/titanium-slag-production/)

### **Other raw material sources**

Natural and synthetic rutile, as well as ore fines, have secondary importance.

## Applications of titanium dioxide.

Due to its very high whiteness and fine particle size, titanium dioxide has found wide application as a white pigment in the paint and coatings industry. Among its advantages are non-toxicity, high optical properties (ability to scatter light), availability, chemical inertness, resistance to atmospheric conditions, and more. Gone are the days when paints were made using zinc or lead-containing white pigments.

### Paint and coatings industry

It is the primary industry using titanium dioxide pigment. But not the last one.

TiO2 is widely used as a white pigment in the pulp and paper industry for producing synthetic fibers, rubber products, plastics, heat-resistant and optical glass, ceramic dielectrics, etc.

## Applications of titanium dioxide other than pigment production are as follows:

### **Production of fiber optic products**

Titanium dioxide, with a chemical purity of 99.9998%, is used in producing optical fiber products, medical equipment, and the radio-electronic industry. In manufacturing ultra-pure glasses, titanium dioxide serves as a purity reference.

### Synthetic fibers and textiles

For matting twisted fibre.

### Cosmetics

For protection against ultraviolet radiation in sunblock creams, for higher whitening effect of toothpastes, soaps, etc.

### Food industry

For higher whitening effect in products, for protection of product package color (plastics) against ultraviolet radiation.

### Pharmaceutical industry

For higher whitening effect in pharma products.

### Printing paint

To increase weather resistance of coatings.

### Catalyst

Photocatalyst and inert ceramic base material for active components.

### Nanotechnology

Titanium dioxide nanopowders are used for air purification in cities, in producing nanofiber paper based on TiO2, in hydrogen energy, etc.

### Manufacture of rubber products

### Production of refractories

Coating of welding electrodes and coatings of casting molds.

## Technologies of titanium dioxide production

In global practice, high-dispersion titanium dioxide pigment is produced by the sulfate (sulfuric acid) and chloride methods.

The sulfate method is based on the decomposition of ilmenite concentrates containing 45-56% TiO2 or titanium slags with a content of 75-80% TiO2, with subsequent conversion of titanium sulfates into dioxide.

The chloride method involves the chlorination of natural rutile concentrates, synthetic rutile, or titanium slags with a TiO2 content of 85% and higher, as well as special slags that have undergone additional processing and contain over 92% TiO2.

Considering specific features of both processes of the TiO2 production process, the primary criterion for choosing between the sulfate and chloride methods is the possibility of providing raw materials of the appropriate quality and environmental-related issues.

Both methods make it possible to obtain high-quality products with identical properties.

The approximate distribution of production technologies among manufacturers worldwide is 45% by the sulfate method and 55% by the chloride method.

### The main stages of the TiO2 process by the sulfate and chloride methods are presented in the table.

| Sulfate (sulfuric acid) method | Chloride method |
| --- | --- |
| Drying, grinding concentrate | Drying, grinding concentrate |
| Decomposition | Drying, grinding of coke |
| Reduction of iron 3+ to iron 2+ | Burden mix melting in ore-thermal furnaces |
| Solution purification | Hot metal and slag casting into moulds |
| Pan crystallization | Cooling and  water herdening |
| Centrifugal removal  of copperas | Slag crushing and grinding |
| Vacuum-evaporating | Slag mixing with tar |
| Hydrolysis | Slag briquetting |
| White filtration | Slag chlorination |
| Whitening and salt treatment | Capture of TiCl4 in refrigerators |
| Calcination | 1st rectifivation of  TiCl4 |
| Dry grindin | 2nd rectifivation of TiCl4 |
| Wet grinding | TiCl4 burning |
| Hydraulic classification | TiO2 and Cl2 capture |
| Surface treatment | Surface treatment |

### **Sulfate (sulfuric acid) method of TiO2 production**

The sulfate method was applied in industry in 1931 to produce the anatase form of titanium dioxide and later, in 1941, for production of the rutile form. In this method, the initial raw material – ilmenite concentrate or titanium slag – is dissolved in sulfuric acid, resulting in titanium, iron, and other metal sulfate solutions. Then, basic TiO2 with the necessary particle size is formed after a series of technological transformations, including chemical reduction, purification, precipitation, washing, and calcination. The crystal structure (anatase or rutile form) is controlled during nucleation and calcination.

The equation describes the sulfate method of the titanium dioxide process:

FeTiO3 + 2H2SO4 → TiOSO4 + FeSO4 + 2H2O TiOSO4 + H2O → TiO2 + H2SO4.

### ****The process diagram of TiO2 production using the sulfate method (with ilmenite as a raw material)****

### **The process diagram of titanium dioxide production using the sulfate method (with titanium slag as a raw material).**

### **Chloride method of TiO2 production**

The chloride method was invented in 1950 to produce the rutile form of TiO2.

The chloride method converts rutile (natural or synthetic) or titanium slag into titanium tetrachloride (TiCl4) through chlorination in the presence of petroleum coke. Any resulting impurities of other metal chlorides are subsequently removed. The following equation describes the chloride method for obtaining TiO2:

2FeTiO3 + 7CI2 + ЗС → 2TiCI4 + 2FeCI3 + 3CO2TiCI4 + O2 → TiO2 + 2CI2.

The most crucial operation in TiO2 production by the chloride method is the combustion of titanium tetrachloride. It is carried out at temperatures between 900-1000°C with burners of a particular design.

The titanium tetrachloride combustion reaction is as follows:

TiCl4 + O2= TiO2 + 2С12.

The released chlorine can be returned to the production process to obtain titanium tetrachloride.

### **Three main methods for obtaining titanium dioxide from its titanium tetrachloride:**

* Hydrolysis of aqueous solutions of titanium tetrachloride (followed by heat treatment of the sediment);
* Vapor-phase hydrolysis of titanium tetrachloride (is based on the interaction of titanium tetrachloride vapors with water vapors). The process is typically carried out at temperatures of 900-1000°C;
* Heat treatment of tetrachloride (combustion in a stream of oxygen).

Titanium pigments obtained by combustion of titanium tetrachloride may contain up to 0.6% adsorbed chlorine. The aqueous suspension of such a product has a pH of less than 7 and is unsuitable for producing paints. Desorption of chlorine from the pigment can be achieved by heating it at temperatures 300-900 °C. The chlorine concentration is reduced to 0.1% in this process. Such a product is suitable for manufacturing paints and enamels but requires surface treatment with silicon and aluminum compounds to obtain higher-quality pigments.

The chloride method is selective and demanding in terms of raw materials. Due to the use of chlorine and high temperatures, it requires corrosion-resistant equipment.

## Comparative characteristics of two methods of titanium dioxide production

In both technological processes – sulfate and chloride – the intermediate products are accumulations of TiO2 crystals of pigment size, which need to be separated (ground) to achieve optimal optical characteristics.

Depending on the end-user requirements, various processing methods are used to modify TiO2, including sedimentation of oxides of silicon, aluminum, zirconium, or zinc onto the surface of pigment fractions.

Particular processing methods may be used to optimize operational characteristics for specific applications utilizing oxides in aqueous or anhydrous environments or various combinations thereof. Additionally, organic additives can be introduced by multiple methods to enhance particular characteristics of the pigment.

### Advantages of the chloride method:

* High TiO2 quality;
* Reduced number of production stages and waste compared to the sulfate method.

### Disadvantages of the chloride method:

* High requirements for raw materials – the use of natural rutile concentrates, synthetic rutile or titanium slags with a TiO2 content of 85% or more as raw materials, as well as special slags that have undergone additional processing and contain more than 92% TiO2;
* Extremely complicated organization of work with chlorine and the need to take measures to prevent chlorine losses;
* The complexity of organizing and recycling ferric chloride and impurities found in the slag;
* Acute need to use equipment made of expensive corrosion-resistant materials.

### Advantages of the sulfate method:

* The quality of the finished product is not worse than the quality of products produced by the chloride method (by using modern technological solutions at the stage of washing chromophore impurities from hydrated TiO2);
* “Zero” waste production – the possibility of completely recycling all production waste into marketable products. Today, waste disposal after the sulfate method is quite sophisticated. At some factories, sales of products obtained from production waste are comparable to sales volumes of commercial products;
* Manufacturing of main equipment and technological devices is cheaper than implementing the chloride method of TiO2 production.

### **Disadvantages of the sulfate method:**

* Influence of chromophore impurities on the finished product quality indicators;
* Inability to use natural (or artificial) rutile as a raw material;
* Use of modified and slightly modified ilmenite concentrates as raw materials.

## Modern methods of additional processing of titanium dioxide pigment.

Practically, there are hardly any industrially produced pigments made of pure TiO2. Most of them undergo inorganic and, in some cases, organic treatment applied to the surface of TiO2 particles through sedimentation, mechanical mixing, or some other method.

Such surface treatment methods improve one or even several operational properties of the pigment, including ease of dispersion, resistance to atmospheric influences, or color stability.

A universal surface treatment method for obtaining a pigment suitable for any practical application has yet to be found. Therefore, the goal of ongoing research is to continue developing new grades of TiO2 that would meet the constantly changing requirements of modern industry.

Titanium dioxide production is a fascinating scientific and technical research and innovation area. Recently, a technology for producing TiO2 has been developed in which ammonium fluoride is used as the primary reagent and is safer than sulfuric acid. Besides, this reagent can be reused, leading to a reduction in waste. One disadvantage of the fluoride technology is that it results in a coarser-dispersed pigment powder compared to the chloride method.

## FAQ

How is titanium dioxide produced?

Titanium dioxide is produced by two methods – sulfate (sulfuric acid) and chloride.

What are the key steps in the chemical processing of titanium dioxide?

The main stages of chemical processing of titanium dioxide, depending on the chosen technology for its production, are as follows:

1. sulfate (sulfuric acid) method – decomposition of the concentrate with reduction of iron 3+ to iron 2+; solution purification, vacuum-crystallization; removal of vitriol in centrifuges; vacuum-evaporation; hydrolysis; white filtration; whitening and salt treatment; calcination; dry and wet grinding; hydraulic classification; surface treatment;
2. chloride method – grinding concentrate and coke; smelting the burden mix in ore-thermal furnaces; casting hot metal and slag into moulds; crushing, grinding slag and mixing it with tar; chlorination of slag with production of titanium tetrachloride TiCl4; 1st and 2nd TiCl4 rectification; TiCl4 combustion; TiO2 and Cl2 capture; surface treatment.

How are the titanium dioxide particles processed into a usable pigment?

Depending on the end user’s requirements and in order to optimize characteristics for specific applications, titanium dioxide is subjected to a so-called surface treatment. A universal method of surface treatment that would make it possible to obtain the most suitable pigment for any practical application, has not been found yet.

Methods of surface treatment are divided into inorganic (sedimentation of aluminum, silicon, zirconium or zinc oxides on the surface of pigment fractions), organic (treatment with organic SAWs – polyols, amines, siloxanes, phosphated fatty acids, etc.), their various combinations.

In general, titanium dioxide surface treatment is necessary to increase the pigment resistance to external influences. The denser is the surface treatment layer, the better are the pigment protective properties. Inorganic treatment increases the resistance of titanium dioxide particles to acid attack. Organic treatment improves pigment particles distribution throughout the composition.

What are the environmental considerations during titanium dioxide production?

Due to its inertness titanium dioxideis non-toxic and is considered a safe substance. It can come into contact with packaged food, and in certain concentrations it can also be used as a food colorant.

Industrial production technology of titanium dioxide is developed taking into account compliance with environmental standards. «M Heavy Technology» offers design services for pigment titanium dioxide producing, using the sulfate method with “zero” waste, i.e. with the possibility of complete processing of all production waste into marketable products.

How is the manufactured titanium dioxide used in various industries?

Titanium dioxide is used as a white pigment in paint and varnish industry, pulp and paper industry, in production of synthetic fibers, rubber products, plastics, heat-resistant and optical glass and ceramic dielectrics.

# We make titanium dioxide. And if we do say so, we’re pretty brilliant at it.

Tronox mines and processes **titanium ore, zircon, rare earths and** **other materials** and manufactures titanium dioxide pigment, specialty-grade titanium dioxide products and high-purity titanium chemicals.  
Our products add brightness and durability to paints, coatings, inks, plastics, paper and a vast array of everyday items.

## From Mine to Pigment

“*From Mine to Pigment*” captures the wide scope and vertical integration of our global operations. At Tronox, we realize the mark we leave behind extends beyond the minerals we extract or the products we manufacture. Operating safely and responsibly is integral to how we do business, and it enables us to safely deliver high-quality titanium dioxide (TiO2) pigment, specialty TiO2 and zircon products for our customers.

At Tronox, we responsibly transform the earth’s resources into products and
opportunities that enhance lives.

Our commitment to sustainability supports our overall vision and strategy to be the world’s leading vertically integrated TiO2 producer.

## Our Products of Technological Innovation

Tronox products span a broad cross-section of industries. Many of the everyday quality-of-life products around us—coatings, paper, plastics, titanium metal—contain components from Tronox.

Relying on global reach and a strong scientific base, CristalACTiV™ products are at the core of technologies that contribute to creating a cleaner world and high-performing applications.

Tronox is the world’s largest supplier of titanium chemicals (TiCl4 and its derivatives), and we have developed a range of high-purity titanium chemicals in various chemical forms and in a broad range of packaging types.

The process of manufacturing TiO2 results in many secondary products. These products range from acids, salts, solids, liquids and gases used within a variety of industries.

## Titanium dioxide is only part of our titanium leadership.

With approximately 5,700 employees across six continents, our rich diversity, unmatched vertical integration, and unparalleled operational and technical expertise across the value chain, position Tronox as the preeminent titanium dioxide producer in the world.

## Sustainability at Tronox

Tronox is a global leader in the mining, production and marketing of inorganic minerals and chemicals. Our business requires an unwavering focus on sustainable operating practices in every sense of the word. We believe we must operate both profitably and sustainably, and we believe these goals are complementary, not in opposition. Our commitment to sustainability supports our overall vision and strategy to be the world’s leading vertically integrated TiO2 producer.

# TDMA – Titanium Dioxide Manufacturers Association

  

The Titanium Dioxide Manufacturers Association (TDMA) – represents the major producers of titanium dioxide (TiO2) and acts as their responsible voice in Europe since 1974 Pure TiO2 is a fine, white powder and is the brightest, whitest pigment available. Highly refractive, ultraviolet absorbing, non-toxic and inert, TiO2 has been used for over 90 years in a vast range of applications including imparting whiteness and opacity to paints, printing inks, plastics, textiles, ceramics, construction materials, cosmetics, food and pharmaceuticals.

TDMA promotes and defends the merits of titanium dioxide (TiO2) in all suitable applications by bringing forward evidence of its safety and efficacy.

TDMA is a non-profit organisation and it has no commercial role. For all commercial enquiries, please refer to the websites of our members.

**CHAIR**

N. Rehman (Tronox)

**SUBSTANCES**

**Core substances:** Titanium dioxide and titanium tetrachloride

[CINKARNA, Metallurgical and Chemical Industry Celje, Inc.](http://www.cinkarna.si/en/) (SI), [KRONOS Worldwide Inc.](http://kronosTiO2.com/) (DE), [LB Group](http://www.lomonbillions.com/) (UK), [PRECHEZA a.s.](https://www.precheza.cz/) (CZ), [TAYCA Corporation](http://www.tayca.co.jp/english/) (JP), [The Chemours Company](https://www.chemours.com/) (USA), [Tronox Holdings plc](http://www.tronox.com/) (NL)

**OBJECTIVES**   
 TDMA strives for the responsible, safe and sustainable manufacture and use of TiO2. It is also ensures that robust scientific information on product safety is made available to authorities and customers and demonstrate that TiO2, in its intended uses, is safe to use in all applications.

Titanium Dioxide is a versatile, high-purity compound renowned for its exceptional whiteness and brightening capabilities. With a chemical composition that ensures optimal opacity and coverage, this fine, white powder is a critical ingredient in a diverse range of applications. In the paint and coatings industry, Titanium Dioxide provides excellent UV resistance and protection, enhancing durability and overall aesthetic appeal. It is also a crucial component in the production of inks, plastics, and fibers, where it imparts superior whiteness and opacity. In the personal care sector, Titanium Dioxide is widely used in sunscreens and cosmetics for its non-toxic, non-reactive properties and its ability to reflect and scatter UV rays, offering excellent photoprotection. Additionally, its food-grade purity makes it suitable as a pigment in food products, contributing to the visual appeal and quality of various consumer goods. This multi-functional ingredient is indispensable across numerous industries, thanks to its reliable performance and safety profile.

# A TiO₂ partner you can trust

##### Ti-Pure™ TiO₂: Quality product, reliable supply, expert service

We drive long-term value for our customers by providing TiO₂ they can count on. For nearly a century, we have produced and delivered high-quality TiO₂ for customers around the globe in coatings, plastics, and laminates applications.

We invented the chloride manufacturing process, and we continue to refine it, to maximize product lifespans and minimize impact on our shared planet. We partner with our customers to help them develop best in class products through the power of TiO₂ innovation.

Each product listed below has what we call a “Grade Guardian” who is responsible for finding and responding to any issues during our production process. If a product doesn’t meet our quality parameters, it doesn’t get shipped.

## Ti-Pure™ for Coatings

Many coatings applications—including architectural, industrial, marine, automotive, aerospace—rely on high-quality TiO₂ to enable opacity, durability, protection, gloss, and bright color. Learn more about [Ti-Pure™ for Coatings](/en/products/coatings).

To find the right grade for your needs, download the [Grade Selection Guide](/en/-/media/files/tipure/tipure-coatings-grade-selection-guide.pdf?rev=59ac10bcc393425e84e1a176a4be4016&hash=50B573B23EF795A0349545305A40C466).

## Ti-Pure™ R-706

This universal grade performs dependably for many demanding applications.

## Ti-Pure™ TS-6706

This universal grade is a TMP/ TME- free version of Ti-Pure™ R-706. Performs dependably for many demanding applications.

## Ti-Pure™ R-900

This versatile TiO₂ pigment adds whiteness and brightness to interior paints.

## Ti-Pure™ R-960

This TiO₂ improves color retention and strengthens weatherability for paints.

## Ti-Pure™ TS-6200

Designed to advance sustainability in the most demanding coating applications by maximizing resource efficiency through extended product life and avoided waste.

## Ti-Pure™ TS-6300

A high-opacity pigment for coatings applications that enables superior hiding power and reduced resource consumption and waste in the painting process.

## Ti-Pure™ R-746

This slurry has good color matching and durability. It maximizes color space.

## Ti-Pure™ R-741

This flat-grade slurry offers superior tint strength and color consistency.

## Ti-Pure™ R-902+

This versatile coating performs well in many end-use applications.

## Ti-Pure™ for Plastics

Plastics applications—including packaging, agricultural, transportation, medical, household appliances, and more—maintain their appearance and strength with the help of TiO₂. Ti-Pure™ solutions for plastics keep products looking newer, longer and resist the damaging effects of UV light. Learn more about [Ti-Pure™ for Plastics](/en/products/plastics).

To find the right grade for your needs, search for [Ti-Pure™ grade recommendations by resin system](/en/applications/plastics) or download the [Grade Selection Guide](/en/-/media/files/tipure/ti-pure-application-guide-plastics-data-sheet.pdf?rev=9fa646165781486c949b124527e4eacf&hash=8B15AB028E7E4283DDB90E91690E60AC).

## Ti-Pure™ R-101

This TiO₂ is ideal for warm, white surfaces, PVC applications, and more.

## Ti-Pure™ R-103

This TiO₂ offsets polymer yellowing for a clean, bright white look.

## Ti-Pure™ R-104

This TiO₂ pigment helps develop bright white plastic with less pigment.

## Ti-Pure™ R-105

This TiO₂ delivers clean, bright whites for outdoor plastic applications.

## Ti-Pure™ R-350

This product has optical performance and brighter, cleaner whites.

## Ti-Pure™ R-960

This product provides outstanding durability for exterior color applications.

## Ti-Pure™ TS-1510

Designed with a new level of processing efficiency that will help masterbatchers reduce their environmental footprints. This pigment provides improved flowability, line productivity, energy, and labor efficiencies along with low-dusting that promotes safer handling.

## Ti-Pure™ for Laminates

The Ti-Pure™ solution for laminates helps beautify and customize homes by adding light stability, color retention, and opacity to laminates used in flooring, furniture, and beyond. Learn more about [Ti-Pure™ for Laminates](/en/products/laminates).
